dismissed_hits.reason: Its counterexamples concern an ill-typed, order-swapped direct/inverse-image composition. The parent instead uses ordered finite-state recurrences justified by prefix-count induction, and the audit verified them; no proof change is needed.

Its warning about cancellation in a saturated semiring is applicable in principle but already addressed: the parent never cancels or divides, and uses only the explicitly proved saturation identities for addition and multiplication.

Its obstruction concerns extending a polynomial-sequence construction to rings without unity. Here the finite saturated counting semiring explicitly has 0 and 1, and no claim about non-unital rings is made.

Its counterexample concerns treating a repairable temporal prefix as permanently rejecting. The restoration automaton retains every carry-count outcome until the finite input ends and tests uniqueness only at the terminal state, as independently audited.
Its inconsistency result concerns a self-containing type universe. The proof uses only explicitly finite state sets and assumes no universe collapse.
Its counterexample refutes continuity and interval-surjectivity for an atomic measure. The restoration argument is a discrete exact recurrence and invokes neither continuity nor surjectivity.
This is a lexical collision involving restoration: its witness concerns graph distances after restoring an edge, while the target concerns digit restoration and makes no graph-distance claim.
Its witness concerns reversing Euler circuits and deleting graph edges. No Euler-circuit, edge-deletion, or closed-trail inference occurs here.

Its warning concerns incorrect operational evaluation of an aliased array assignment. The column recurrence uses distinct cell variables and the exact carry equation; fresh literal enumeration again agreed with the lifted automaton.
Its electrical-network counterexample refutes a resistance lower bound derived from distance and degree. Neither effective resistance nor an analogous inequality is used in this proof.

Its counterexample concerns omitted dependence between family size and a probability parameter. The restoration counts are exact finite combinatorial counts with no probabilistic independence assumption.

Its reduction-asymmetry warning is already respected: the parity reduction is explicitly constructed in the needed direction, and the polynomial-time many-one completeness observation is separately labeled vacuous.

Its warning is that equivalence depends on the chosen observable. Here the observable is exactly the nested uniqueness semantics, and the audit plus fresh literal enumeration compared that semantics directly with the automaton.

Its witness concerns an erroneous binary-to-decimal digit estimate. The parent makes no such estimate and states both its running time and projection relative to the source convention and a fixed natural encoding.
Its counterexample exposes an invalid padding-and-pigeonhole reduction. Neither the automaton proof nor the parity projection uses padding, average occupancy, or a pigeonhole inference.

Its warning concerns a failed probabilistic transition bound at a boundary state. Initial carry 0, both terminal carries, empty type groups, and the empty-column boundary were checked explicitly here and in the audit.

results.claim: Counts may be truncated to {0,1,2} without losing any information relevant to level-3 restoration.
results.proof_sketch: Let D={0,1,2}, where 2 means “at least two”, with a⊕b=min(2,a+b) and a⊗b=min(2,ab). For h(r)=min(2,r) on nonnegative integers, direct case analysis gives h(a+b)=h(a)⊕h(b) and h(ab)=h(a)⊗h(b). Thus h is a semiring homomorphism. Every transfer count is formed solely by nonnegative sums and products, so saturation preserves exactly whether a count is zero, one, or greater than one. In particular, every equality-to-one test introduced by a uniqueness quantifier is preserved.

results.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is decidable in O(m n^3) time under the source paper’s complexity convention.
results.proof_sketch: For column i, fix its local type-3 tuple x and type-2 tuple y. Let A_i(x,y) be the 2-by-2 matrix whose carry-to-carry entry is the saturated number of local type-1 tuples satisfying the column equation. Starting from q_0=(1,0), induction shows that q_i=q_{i-1}A_i(x_i,y_i) gives the saturated number of type-1 prefixes ending with each carry. Hence the inner uniqueness predicate holds exactly when q_m(α)=1. There are nine q-states. For fixed x, form a 9-by-9 matrix B_i(x) whose p,q entry counts local type-2 tuples y satisfying pA_i(x,y)=q. Starting with d_0 concentrated at (1,0), induction shows that d_i=d_{i-1}B_i(x_i) counts type-2 prefixes producing each q-state. Thus the saturated sum of d_m(q) over q with q(α)=1 equals one exactly when the two nested uniqueness predicates hold. Type-3 tuples give existential transitions in the layered graph of the constant 3^9 possible d-states. A column has at most three variable cells, so all combined local tuples number at most n^3; every state-space factor is constant.

results.claim: The same construction places every fixed-level additive restoration problem in P.
results.proof_sketch: Suppose the predicate remaining after lower types have been eliminated is recognized by a deterministic N-state automaton. Eliminating the next globally unique type replaces a state by its vector in {0,1,2}^N of saturated assignment counts ending in each old state. Local transitions sum over that type’s local digit choices, and acceptance tests whether the saturated total over accepting old states equals one. The semiring invariant and induction over columns give the exact nested-uniqueness semantics, so the lifted automaton has at most 3^N states. Beginning with the two carry states and repeating for each inner type yields N_0=2 and N_{j+1}≤3^{N_j}. For every fixed level this tower depends only on the level, not on m or n. The outer existential type is handled by layered reachability, and a column still has only three cells, leaving at most n^3 combined local assignments up to a level-dependent constant.

results.claim: For every fixed level and fixed base, additive restoration is a regular language of column words under the natural encoding.
results.proof_sketch: Fix the level k and base n. The iterated counting lift in the preceding claim leaves a finite state set Q, depending only on k, after all inner uniquely quantified types have been eliminated. The alphabet of three-cell columns is also finite once k and n are fixed. Reading least-significant column first, a column symbol σ and an assignment a to its local type-k cells give a deterministic map τ_{σ,a}:Q→Q. Make a finite NFA with state set Q and, on σ, all transitions q→τ_{σ,a}(q). Distinct restoration blanks are local to their cells, so choosing one such transition in every column is exactly choosing a complete outer type-k assignment. The counting-lift invariant proves that an endpoint is accepting exactly when the remaining nested uniqueness formula holds; the prescribed terminal carry merely selects one of two fixed accepting sets. Thus the NFA recognizes precisely the original level-k semantics. Powerset determinization gives a DFA independent of the number of columns, proving regularity. An encoding that lists columns most-significant first recognizes the reversal, which is regular as well. Equivalently, acceptance is a product of constant-size Boolean transition matrices. The automaton may depend on n, so this claim does not assert regularity uniformly over a varying base.

results.claim: Under the natural column encoding, EVEN PARITY reduces to level-3 additive restoration by a constant-block projection, already in base 2 with no type-3 cells.
results.proof_sketch: Process columns from least to most significant and require final carry 0. Put A=(0,1,*_1), B=(*_1,*_1,*_1), C=(0,1,*_2), where *_j is a type-j blank. Use I=AA for input bit 0 and T=BC for input bit 1, after one fixed I prefix. In the audited d-state semantics, A has identity carry matrix. B has saturated matrix [[2,1],[1,2]], while C sends q=(a,b), for its two type-2 choices, to (a,0) and (0,b). Exact multiplication gives five sparse d-states D0={(1,0):1}, D1={(0,1):1,(2,0):1}, D2={(0,2):2,(1,0):1,(2,0):1}, D3={(0,1):1,(0,2):2,(2,0):2}, and D4={(0,2):2,(1,0):1,(2,0):2}. I fixes every Dj, while T maps D0→D1→D2→D3→D4→D3. The terminal carry-0 predicate holds exactly at D0,D2,D4, so acceptance is equivalent to even Hamming weight. Empty type 3 has its unique empty assignment. With a fixed binary code for the base-2 cell alphabet, every output bit is a constant or a literal of one input bit, establishing the claimed projection.

results.claim: Under the natural column encoding, level-3 additive restoration is not in AC0, even when restricted to base 2.
results.proof_sketch: EVEN PARITY is not in AC0. If the base-2 restriction of level-3 additive restoration were in AC0, composing that circuit family with the constant-block projection of the preceding claim would put EVEN PARITY in AC0, a contradiction. The unrestricted language contains this restriction, and the same reduction targets valid unrestricted instances, so it too is not in AC0 under the same encoding.

results.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is formally P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, but this vacuous completeness convention does not provide the requested matching hardness classification.
results.proof_sketch: Membership in P follows from the transfer algorithm. The language is nontrivial: in base 2 with one column and required final carry 0, [type-3 x]+0=0 is YES by choosing x=0, while [type-3 x]+1=0 is NO because x=0 has the wrong result digit and x=1 has final carry 1. For every L in P, a polynomial-time reduction can decide whether its input belongs to L and output these fixed YES or NO instances. This formally proves P-hardness under polynomial-time many-one reductions, but exactly the same argument applies to every nontrivial language in P. It therefore supplies no structural lower bound. No logspace or comparably restrictive P-hardness reduction is established, so the meaningful matching-hardness part of the target remains unresolved.

final_writeup:
Let h(r)=min(2,r). On nonnegative integers, h preserves addition and multiplication when the codomain {0,1,2} uses saturated operations. Thus all completion counts may be stored exactly as zero, one, or at least two—the only distinctions tested by the nested uniqueness quantifiers.

For fixed type-3 and type-2 digits, process the m internal columns from least to most significant. Let q_i(c) be the saturated number of type-1 assignments in the first i columns that satisfy those columns and leave carry c∈{0,1}. Initialize q_0=(1,0). For each column, a two-by-two transfer matrix records, for every incoming and outgoing carry, the saturated number of compatible local type-1 tuples. Induction over columns proves the stated meaning of q_i. Consequently, q_m(α)=1 exactly when the fixed type-2 assignment has a unique type-1 completion with prescribed final carry α. There are only 3^2=9 possible q-states.

For fixed type-3 digits, lift the construction once. Let d_i(q) be the saturated number of type-2 prefixes through column i that produce first-level state q. Its transition sums over the local type-2 tuples and applies the corresponding first-level transfer. A second induction proves this invariant. At the last column, the saturated sum of d_m(q) over states satisfying q(α)=1 equals one exactly when there is a unique complete type-2 assignment having a unique type-1 completion. There are 3^9 possible d-states. Finally, type-3 choices are existential, so their local tuples induce ordinary reachability through the layered graph of d-states. An accepting path exists exactly when the level-3 formula ∃v3:∃!v2:∃!v1 is true.

Keeping only carry transitions that are locally unique would be unsound. With two base-2 columns, all six cells type 1, and final carry 0, the carry path 0→1→0 has one local filling in each column, but the puzzle has ten global fillings: nine through intermediate carry 0 and one through intermediate carry 1. The count-vector construction retains the information needed to reject it.

All state-space sizes above are absolute constants. Each column contains only three cells, so enumerating all combined local digit tuples costs at most n^3. The resulting running time is O(m n^3) under the source paper’s convention. More generally, eliminating another globally unique type replaces an N-state automaton by at most 3^N saturated-count states. Therefore every fixed-level additive restoration problem lies in P, although its level-dependent constant grows as a finite tower.

Fixing the base as well as the level gives a sharper structural consequence. After the inner unique types are eliminated, the remaining state set is finite. A column and one local assignment to its outermost blanks specify a transition on that state set; allowing all such assignments makes a finite NFA. Outer assignments are exactly its paths, and the counting invariant makes its accepting paths exactly the valid nested restorations. Thus every fixed-level, fixed-base restriction is a regular language of column words (equivalently, a product of constant-size Boolean transition matrices). This does not assert one finite automaton for all varying bases. In particular, the base-2 level-3 restriction is regular, while the reduction below shows that it is not in AC0.

There is also a direct, nonvacuous lower-bound construction. Work in base 2, prescribe final carry 0, and use no type-3 cells. In least-to-most-significant order define A=(0,1,*_1), B=(*_1,*_1,*_1), and C=(0,1,*_2), where *_j denotes a type-j blank. Encode an input bit 0 by the two-column block I=AA and a bit 1 by T=BC, after one fixed I prefix.

The transfer effects can be checked completely. A has the identity carry matrix. B has saturated carry matrix [[2,1],[1,2]]. For C, its two type-2 choices send q=(a,b) to (a,0) and (0,b). Starting from d-state D0={(1,0):1}, the only states reached by bit blocks are
D1={(0,1):1,(2,0):1},
D2={(0,2):2,(1,0):1,(2,0):1},
D3={(0,1):1,(0,2):2,(2,0):2}, and
D4={(0,2):2,(1,0):1,(2,0):2},
with unlisted coordinates zero. The block I fixes all five states, while T maps D0→D1→D2→D3→D4→D3. Terminal carry 0 accepts exactly D0,D2,D4. Therefore the constructed puzzle is accepted exactly when the input has even Hamming weight. The empty type-3 group has its sole empty assignment, so these are valid level-3 instances. Under any fixed binary code for the natural base-2 column alphabet, each input bit merely selects one of two fixed equal-length blocks; this is an AC0 many-one reduction, indeed a constant-block projection, from EVEN PARITY. Thus, under this natural encoding, the base-2 restriction and the full problem are not in AC0.

This lower bound is meaningful but still does not match the polynomial-time upper bound. For completeness, the language is formally P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions because a reduction may decide any source language in P and select fixed YES or NO restoration instances. That observation applies to every nontrivial language in P and supplies no structural lower bound. No logspace or comparably restrictive P-hardness reduction, nor another tight classification between the parity obstruction and P, is proved here. The correct claimed resolution therefore remains PARTIAL: level 3, and indeed every fixed level, is in P, and level 3 is already parity-hard under AC0 reductions, but meaningful matching hardness remains unresolved.
